source.title: Implicit Regularization in Deep Learning May Not Be Explainable by Norms

record.file_problem: Whole paper text is present. Some plot values are figure-only, with no numerical values stated in the text.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests implicit regularization in matrix and tensor completion, but does not measure natural-label test error, the generalization gap, sharpness, or any other behavior named in V1–V8.
record.gate_note: The study's results on norms, effective rank, and tensor rank concern fitted completion solutions and training loss or reconstruction error, not the claim versions' specified held-out generalization findings. It also cites prior work on generalization; those cited results are not this study's results.
record.test_reason: The study tests norm minimization and low-rank implicit bias in matrix and tensor completion. Its reconstruction results measure generalization, but none tests the specific comparisons or behaviors in V1–V8. Diverging norms do not test V7's magnitude-aware sharpness correlation.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is broadly accurate. The authors establish matrix-completion settings where implicit regularization drives all norms and quasi-norms of the product matrix upward without bound while essentially minimizing rank. They favor rank over norm minimization as an interpretation, demonstrate a low-rank tendency empirically in tensor factorization, and hypothesize relevance to contemporary networks. Their result affirms Conjecture 2 but does not formally refute Conjecture 1 because its technical assumptions need not hold.
record.recipe_differences: The experiments use matrix and tensor completion with gradient descent and report loss, reconstruction error, norms, and rank-related properties. They do not use the natural-data classification or held-out test-error methods in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The Figure 1 caption says depth, balancedness, and small learning rate and initialization contribute to the matrix-factorization effect; the transition from depth 2 to 3 or more is most significant. Tensor-factorization rank tendency is stronger with smaller initialization.

fits_no_version.finding: For constructed completion problems, balanced gradient flow with the required initial determinant sign drives every norm and quasi-norm of the product matrix to infinity if loss approaches zero, while effective rank approaches its infimum and distance to infimal rank approaches zero. Experiments illustrate this behavior with sensitivity to depth, initialization, learning rate, and observation perturbations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Implicit regularization in matrix factorization need not minimize any norm or quasi-norm of the learned mapping and can instead favor approximate low rank.

fits_no_version.finding: Unconstrained tensor factorization trained from small random initialization tends toward low estimated CP-rank and accurately reconstructs low-rank ground truth in the tested settings; smaller initialization strengthens the tendency.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gradient descent on overparameterized tensor factorizations can favor low-rank solutions and generalize to unobserved tensor entries.

record.problems: The experiments use synthetic matrix or tensor completion rather than natural-data classification. Matrix-factorization plots report representative runs, and the text supplies no plotted numerical values. Tensor experiments report five trials per initialization standard deviation with interquartile-range error bars, but the plotted numerical outcomes are not stated in the text. The matrix-factorization theoretical analysis assumes gradient flow and balanced initialization; extensions to unbalanced initialization are qualified by technical conditions.
record.rows_left_out: No additional qualifying findings were omitted. The study's theoretical bounds and propositions are recorded in fits_no_version rather than as separate intervention-result rows; the plots' numerical points are figure-only and unavailable as stated text values.

untested.parts: Coexistence of random-label fitting and natural-label generalization, including chance-level held-out accuracy on random labels.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classification performance and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove the penalty.
Dropout effects on held-out classification error across data sizes and regularization settings.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, its correlation with generalization gaps, and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Test-accuracy effects of removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: States are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8 because all rows are outside those versions; this does not deny the reported completion effects. Tensor reconstruction measures generalization, so lack of classification alone is not the exclusion reason. Tensor experiments use fixed, unconstrained factorization widths rather than width sweeps, and their linear baseline is not a fully connected image classifier.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label held-out accuracy.
Width sweeps and test error beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to the train-test gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring test accuracy.

rows.subject: matrix factorization
rows.operation_detail: Depth 3 gradient descent with perturbed or repositioned observations.

conditions.value: sign accords with product of adjacent observations

rows.measure: Absolute value of unobserved entry as loss decreases
rows.value: Figure only; text says the unobserved entry grows when the diagonally opposite observation is zero, and the growth recedes as that observation is perturbed away from zero.
rows.note: The caption reports representative runs and says other evaluated settings produced similar results.
rows.check: Perturbation sensitivity does not measure any version. Correct the determinant condition: its sign matches the adjacent-observation product for a diagonal missing entry and is opposite for an off-diagonal missing entry. Section C.2.1 reports negative initial determinants for Figure 5.
